analysis.summary: Primary foreground object is a black wired Lenovo optical mouse on a white surface, shown from a top-rear angle with curved ergonomic shell, red scroll wheel, and attached black cable extending out of frame.

components.name: Main housing shell
components.function: Forms ergonomic body that supports hand and encloses internal elements
components.evidence: Matte black curved dome with white Lenovo logo on rear hump visible on white background

components.name: Left and right click buttons
components.evidence: Two front zones defined by thin seam lines diverging from scroll wheel on top surface

components.name: Scroll wheel
components.function: Allows vertical scrolling or secondary input via rotation and press
components.evidence: Small red textured wheel centered between button seams at front of mouse

components.name: Attached cable
components.function: Physical tether for power and data connection to computer
components.evidence: Thin black flexible cord exiting front center of mouse and curving across white surface

components.name: Side contour panels
components.function: Define grip area and lateral shape of housing
components.evidence: Darker glossy side wall visible along left flank of mouse beneath matte top shell

principles.name: Depressible button input
principles.explanation: Visible seams suggest top front sections can flex downward, likely to actuate internal switches beneath for click input; switch type not visible and remains inferred.

principles.name: Rotational scroll input
principles.explanation: Exposed red wheel position between buttons is consistent with a scroll control that translates finger-driven rotation into scroll commands; internal encoder not visible.

principles.name: Wired power and data interface
principles.explanation: Attached cord indicates reliance on physical connection rather than battery/radio, likely carrying both power and signal between mouse and host device; connector and protocol not shown.

principles.name: Ergonomic surface shaping
principles.explanation: Asymmetric curved dome and sloped sides provide a contoured contact surface that distributes hand pressure and guides finger placement.

uncertainty: Underside sensor type, feet, labeling and tracking technology not visible in this top view
Internal construction including switches, encoders, circuit board and sensor not observable
Cable termination connector type, length and condition not shown
Exact material composition, surface finish and manufacturing method cannot be verified from photo alone
Precise dimensions, weight and right- or left-hand specific ergonomics not determinable
Functional condition, responsiveness or wear cannot be assessed from a static image

safety_notes: Low-voltage peripheral but avoid exposure to liquids, heat or cable damage

Clean only exterior with dry or lightly damp cloth when disconnected, per manufacturer guidance
